opener.evidence: Frame 1 is self-contained: it shows the title “Graphs: How AI understands relationships,” a tablet with separate topic/video cards, the notebook line “Nodes + edges connect video topics,” and a sticky note example “recommend the next study video.” A viewer can understand the lesson topic, the school graph idea, and the AI recommendation example from the opener alone.

native_composition.evidence: All eight frames share a coherent warm study-desk world with the recurring Indian learner in a green/teal shirt, lamp, books, notebook, sticky notes, pen cup, and tablet as the teaching surface. Diagrams and text appear inside tablet UIs, notebooks, sticky notes, and poster-style brush headings rather than on blank corporate slides.

overlay_risk.evidence: Most text appears integrated into the scene, especially tablet labels, notebook writing, and sticky notes. However, several large white brush-stroke headline areas in frames 1, 5, 6, 7, and 8 read somewhat like graphic title bands placed over the illustration. They are stylistically consistent and not plain rectangular overlays, but the risk is visible.

mechanism_visibility.evidence: The sequence visibly shows the mechanism: separate video cards in frame 1, item-to-node transformation in frame 2, relationship edges in frame 3, a graph/network in frame 4, connected neighbors in frame 5, a highlighted path to recommendation in frame 6, a knowledge graph in frame 7, and a path-supported choice versus dim unconnected cricket option in frame 8.

mobile_readability.evidence: The main teaching text and key labels are readable in the contact sheet: “Each item becomes a node,” “Relationships become edges,” “Nodes + edges form a graph,” “Connected neighbors are related,” “A path can explain a recommendation,” “knowledge graph,” and the quick-check choices. Some small tablet/notebook details are tight, but the essential mechanism labels remain legible.

frame_notes.evidence: Strong opener with title, learner, tablet topic cards, notebook graph doodle, and sticky-note example. Separate items are visible with no edges yet.
Clearly shows video/topic labels transforming into colored circular nodes with arrows. “node” callout is large, and no graph edges are shown yet.
Shows related items connected by glowing edges on the tablet, with “Relationships become edges,” “edge,” and “related” visible. Unrelated cards/icons remain separate.
Tablet displays a compact graph/network with connected nodes, and notebook text states “Nodes + edges form a graph.” The learner points at the graph, reinforcing the teaching step.
Shows “AI basics” connected to “machine learning” and “coding tutorial,” with related labels attached to the visible edges. Far nodes are dimmed.
A highlighted path runs from “AI basics” through “machine learning” to “coding tutorial,” with “path” and “recommend” labels visible. The recommendation is explained by the visible route.
Broadens the concept to a knowledge graph on the tablet with icons, connected nodes, and readable labels “knowledge graph,” “node,” and “edge.”
Quick-check frame clearly contrasts a connected “coding tutorial” choice with a dimmed “cricket highlights” choice. The visible path from “AI basics” supports the correct recommendation.

verdict.verdict: Acceptable native image-story set. It successfully teaches the graph mechanism through visible nodes, edges, paths, and recommendation evidence in a consistent warm student/tablet scene. Minor caveat: the large brush-stroke headline areas have some overlay-like risk, but they are not severe enough to block use.
